canvas-01-1.description: The main map on the title sheet (printed sheet 1), drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, covering the south-western shore of Grenloch Lake east of Eastview Avenue. It occupies the lower left of the page below the key map and index, and is enclosed by heavy lines. Central Avenue runs along the top from Eastview Avenue and bends north-east past the end of Private Road towards the bridge at the head of the lake; Lake Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from Eastview Avenue to the road that follows the lake shore, and a 12 ft alley numbered 105 runs along the bottom. Block 107, between Central Avenue and Lake Avenue, and the block south of Lake Avenue are laid out in narrow numbered lots, most of them empty; a few one- and two-story frame dwellings, a store, automobile sheds and a storage building stand near Eastview Avenue and Lake Avenue. The large lot north of block 107 holds the compass rose, two small buildings and, near Private Road, the 40,000 gallon wood tank on a 100 ft steel tower of the water works, with 4 and 6 inch water pipes. Frame buildings stand on the narrow strip between Central Avenue and the lake at the upper right. Grenloch Lake fills the right edge of the part, with the shore road between it and the blocks. Street widths are marked as 80 ft for Central Avenue, 60 ft for Lake Avenue and 50 ft for Eastview Avenue. Sheet 2 adjoins on the left beyond Eastview Avenue and sheet 4 at the top.
notes: The road along the lake shore is lettered only Road; it has no counterpart in OpenStreetMap, and Lake Avenue now ends short of the lake.
Placed from Eastview Avenue / Central Avenue and Eastview Avenue / Lake Avenue (detected) and three points carried from sheet 4 around the water tank.

Printed sheet 1. Title page with water/fire notes, key, location map, street and specials index and a key map at 600 ft to an inch (not configured), plus two 50 ft map parts: part 1 (lower left) Eastview Av, Central Av, Lake Av and the west shore of Grenloch Lake with the road along it; part 2 (inset, lower right) Asyla Rd / Black Horse Pike / Davistown Rd with the Public Service Corp. auto bus garage. Scale 50 ft. Part 1: 2 detected junctions on Eastview Av plus 3 points carried from sheet 4. Part 2: anchored on Black Horse Pike / Davistown Rd / Lakeland Rd (old Asyla Rd), scale from part 1, low confidence.

canvas-01-2.description: An inset on the title sheet (printed sheet 1), drawn at 50 feet to an inch and enclosed by heavy lines at the lower right of the page, showing the crossing of Black Horse Pike with Asyla Road and Davistown Road at the north-eastern edge of Grenloch, away from the rest of the mapped area; the key map places it on the pike north-east of the village. The pike runs up the page, turned so that north points towards the upper right, as its own north arrow shows. The only building of note is the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey auto bus garage on the north-east corner, a cement block building with a cement block office, capacity five busses, heated by stove and lit by electricity, with a concrete floor and gasoline tanks along the pike. A frame dwelling and an automobile shed stand on the north-west corner, with chicken coops behind them; the other corners are marked vacant beyond. Street widths are marked as 50 ft for the pike and 40 ft for Asyla Road and Davistown Road.
notes: Asyla Road is now Lakeland Road (OpenStreetMap).
Placed on the single junction Black Horse Pike / Davistown Road / Lakeland Road, with scale taken from part 1 and rotation from the measured street lines (anchored); low confidence.

sheet-2.description: The south-western residential blocks of Grenloch, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The sheet runs from Central Avenue along the top edge past Lake Avenue to Park Avenue, between County Road to Turnerville on the left and Eastview Avenue on the right, with Linwood Avenue dividing the upper and lower rows of blocks; the Road to Hurfville leaves County Road to Turnerville westward opposite Park Avenue. Blocks 1, 2, 3, 103 and 104 are shown, laid out in narrow numbered lots and split by 12 ft alleys. Housing is mostly one- and two-story frame dwellings with automobile sheds and small outbuildings, thickest along the north side of Park Avenue and along Lake Avenue. Grenloch First Presbyterian Church, heated by furnace and lit by electricity, stands at the corner of Lake Avenue and Eastview Avenue, and the Grenloch Terrace Public School, heated by stove, stands in block 103 south of Park Avenue. Much of block 2 and the southern half of block 104 are vacant. Two dwellings stand west of County Road to Turnerville at the left margin. Street widths are marked as 80 ft for Central Avenue, 60 ft for Lake and Park Avenues and 50 ft for Linwood and Eastview Avenues. Sheet 3 adjoins across Central Avenue at the top, sheet 1 at the right beyond Eastview Avenue.
notes: County Road to Turnerville is now Woodbury-Turnersville Road (OpenStreetMap).
Road to Hurfville is now Hurffville-Grenloch Road (OpenStreetMap).
Linwood Avenue does not reach Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap today.
Central Av, Lake Av, Park Av between County Road to Turnerville and Eastview Av, crossed by Linwood Av; Grenloch First Presbyterian Church, Grenloch Terrace Public School. One part. Scale 50 ft.

sheet-3.description: The north-western residential blocks of Grenloch, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The sheet covers the grid between County Road to Turnerville along the left edge and Eastview Avenue along the right edge, divided by Linwood Avenue down the middle and crossed by Milburn Avenue, Edgewater Avenue and, along the bottom edge, Central Avenue. Blocks 5 to 10 are shown, each split lengthwise by a 12 ft alley and laid out in narrow numbered lots of the Grenloch Terrace plan. Building is thin: scattered one- and two-story frame dwellings, many with automobile sheds, storage sheds and chicken coops in the rear lots, with the most houses on the south side of Edgewater Avenue and along Central Avenue. One dwelling on Edgewater Avenue near Eastview Avenue is of concrete block. Many lots, particularly in blocks 7, 9 and 10, are still vacant. A 6 inch water pipe runs along Linwood Avenue and a 4 inch pipe along Central Avenue, with fire hydrants at Linwood Avenue and at Eastview Avenue. Street widths are marked as 60 ft for Milburn and Edgewater Avenues, 50 ft for Linwood and Eastview Avenues, and 80 ft for Central Avenue. The top of the sheet shows the continuation of the lots north of block 10 and 9 without a street, and the blocks below Central Avenue belong to sheet 2; sheet 4 adjoins on the right beyond Eastview Avenue.
notes: Milburn Avenue is now Milborne Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
County Road to Turnerville is now Woodbury-Turnersville Road (OpenStreetMap).
Milburn Av, Edgewater Av, Central Av between County Road to Turnerville and Eastview Av, crossed by Linwood Av; dwellings. One part. Scale 50 ft. Pilot sheet.

sheet-4.description: The industrial centre of Grenloch, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, between Eastview Avenue on the left edge and Lake View Avenue on the right. Most of the sheet is the works of Bateman and Companies, Inc., noted as in the hands of receivers, plant closed and buildings mostly vacant, with two watchmen, approved clocks, water supply kept up by an electric pump and a hose cart of the village fire company kept near the plant. The works lie in blocks 109, 110 and 111 on both sides of the South Branch of Timber Creek and the mill run or race, which is crossed by a foot bridge; they include the vacant foundry building with its core ovens, a fire-proof concrete building of 1918, numbered warehouses, a repair department, shipping building with concrete platform, bridges between buildings, filter beds and a disposal basin in the upper left. Private Road runs through the plant. Central Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet from Eastview Avenue past the plant, over a concrete bridge at the head of Grenloch Lake, to the P. & R. Ry. Grenloch Branch, whose passenger depot, freight house and coal pockets stand at the right; the post office is on Central Avenue near the bridge. Main crosses the upper right to the railroad, with dwellings and stores in block 112. A hose cart house of concrete block and a few dwellings stand in block 4 along Eastview Avenue, and a 40,000 gallon wood tank on a 100 ft steel tower stands south of Central Avenue. Sheets 3, 1 and 5 adjoin on the left, at the bottom and on the right.
notes: Lake View Avenue north of Central Avenue is now Linden Street, and south of it Lakeview Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Modern Main Street runs south through the old plant site to Central Avenue; the old Main is only its north-eastern end.
Central Avenue crossed the railroad to Lake View Avenue by a 33 ft crossing; the modern Central Avenue / Linden Street junction is about 4 m off the drawn one and was not used.
Central Avenue / Lake View Avenue and Main / Lake View Avenue were hand-picked; the detector found only Central Avenue / Eastview Avenue.
Bateman and Companies, Inc., in the hands of receivers, plant closed.

Bateman & Companies Inc. works (in hands of receivers, mostly vacant) on the South Branch of Timber Creek and the race, between Eastview Av and Lake View Av; Central Av, Main, Private Road, P. & R. Ry. Grenloch Branch with passenger depot, post office, Grenloch Lake. One part. Scale 50 ft. Placed on Central/Eastview (detected) and two hand-picked junctions on Lake View Av (now Linden St / Lakeview Av); exact 3-point affine, medium-low confidence.

sheet-5.description: The eastern part of Grenloch between Poplar Street or Black Horse Pike and Lake View Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points towards the upper left. Main runs down the left side of the sheet and Central Avenue down the middle, both from the pike to Lake View Avenue, and Woodlynne Avenue closes the right side; Lake View Avenue bends where it meets Central Avenue, and a short stub of Central Avenue continues south across the railroad at the bottom. Block 113, between Main and Central Avenue, is cut into long narrow lots running back from both streets, with one- and one-and-a-half-story frame dwellings, mostly along Central Avenue and the lower part of Main, and many lots still vacant. Block 114, between Central Avenue and Woodlynne Avenue, holds a few dwellings, a store, coops and sheds, and its lots fanning out towards the pike are largely empty. North of the pike in block 116 stands the Grenloch Public School, heated by stoves and lit by electricity, with a few frame dwellings and stores at the upper left and the edge of a frame building at the right margin. Dwellings in block 112 west of Main appear at the left margin. Along the bottom the P. & R. Ry. Grenloch Branch runs with its sidings, and the shore of Grenloch Lake appears at the lower right. A 2 inch water pipe runs along part of the pike, down Central Avenue and along Lake View Avenue. Street widths are marked as 50 ft for the pike, Main and Central Avenue and 40 ft for Woodlynne and Lake View Avenues. Sheet 4 adjoins at the bottom.
notes: The pike is lettered Poplar St. or Black Horse Pike; OpenStreetMap has it as Black Horse Pike.
Lake View Avenue west of Central Avenue is now Linden Street, and east of it Lakeview Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Woodlynne Avenue is now Woodlyn Avenue (OpenStreetMap), realigned on a curve at both ends; its junctions were not used.
Main is now Main Street (OpenStreetMap).
Main / Lake View Avenue was hand-picked; the detector did not find it among the railroad lines.

Main, Central Av and Woodlynne Av between Poplar St or Black Horse Pike and Lake View Av; Grenloch Public School, P. & R. Ry. Grenloch Branch along the bottom. Sheet drawn turned (north towards the upper left). One part. Scale 50 ft. Woodlynne Av (now Woodlyn Av) realigned on curves at both ends, left out; Main / Lake View Av hand-picked.
